root_cause.text: A double-free vulnerability in smbd_post_send_iter() occurs when smbd_send_batch_flush() fails after smbd_post_send() has moved the request to the batch list, because smbd_send_batch_flush() already frees the request, yet the code then falls through to smbd_free_send_io() again.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explains: "smbd_send_batch_flush() already calls smbd_free_send_io(), so we should not call it again after smbd_post_send() moved it to the batch list." The patch adds a `goto err_flush` after the flush failure to skip the redundant `smbd_free_send_io()` call at the `err_dma` label.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: A double-free vulnerability in smbd_post_send_iter() occurs when smbd_send_batch_flush() fails after smbd_post_send() has moved the request to the batch list, because smbd_send_batch_flush() already frees the request, yet the code then falls through to smbd_free_send_io() again.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The commit message explains: "smbd_send_batch_flush() already calls smbd_free_send_io(), so we should not call it again after smbd_post_send() moved it to the batch list." The patch adds a `goto err_flush` after the flush failure to skip the redundant `smbd_free_send_io()` call at the `err_dma` label.

candidates.rationale: Moves the request into the batch list. If successful, the request is now managed by the batch and may be freed by smbd_send_batch_flush on failure.
Controls entry into the critical path where smbd_send_batch_flush is called only when smbd_post_send succeeds.
Determines whether the batch flush is skipped. When batch equals &_batch, the flush is executed, leading to potential double-free if it fails.
Flushes the batch. On failure, it may already free the request, making a subsequent free a double-free.
Condition that exits early on success; when rc is non-zero, execution falls through to the double-free path.
Only executed when rc is zero; otherwise control flows to err_dma, enabling the double-free.
Label that marks the fall-through target after the failed flush; execution reaches smbd_free_send_io regardless of whether the request was already freed.
Second free of the request when smbd_send_batch_flush already freed it, causing a double-free vulnerability.

vuln_statements.explanation: Final free performed after smbd_send_batch_flush may have already freed the request, causing a double-free vulnerability when flush fails.
On failure, smbd_send_batch_flush may free the request internally, but the code does not set the request pointer to NULL or prevent the subsequent free at err_dma.
Label that is reached after the flush failure, causing execution to fall through to smbd_free_send_io regardless of whether the request was already freed.
Transfers ownership of the request to the batch; subsequent failure in flush leads to double free because the request is potentially freed by both flush and the err_dma path.
Condition that enters the flush path; the double-free occurs only when this condition is true (i.e., post_send succeeded) and then smbd_send_batch_flush fails.
Controls whether the flush is skipped; when batch equals &_batch, the flush is executed, and its potential failure leads to the double-free.
Early exit when batch is not the local batch; when this is not taken, the flush and subsequent double-free path are followed.
Second check after the flush; when rc is non-zero, execution falls through to err_dma, bypassing the second return and enabling the double free.
